source.original_text: For two normalized exponential tilts of one common base measure, the log density of the left tilt relative to the right tilt is represented by the left exponent minus its log normalizer, minus the right exponent plus its log normalizer. In the restricted-Gaussian application this identity is used under the left fiber law. ASTIS records the equality almost everywhere with the canonical log-likelihood-ratio representative; it does not infer equality of classical gradients.

lean.statement: ∀ {X : Type*} [MeasurableSpace X] (mu : Measure X) [SigmaFinite mu] (f g : X → ℝ), Measurable f → Integrable (fun x => Real.exp (f x)) mu → Integrable (fun x => Real.exp (g x)) mu → llr (mu.tilted f) (mu.tilted g) =ᵐ[mu.tilted f] fun x => f x - Real.log (∫ z, Real.exp (f z) ∂mu) - g x + Real.log (∫ z, Real.exp (g z) ∂mu)

blind_reconstruction.text: For every measurable space X, every sigma-finite measure mu on X, and all functions f,g:X->R, assume that f is measurable and that both x->exp(f(x)) and x->exp(g(x)) are mu-integrable. Define Z_f = integral exp(f(z)) dmu(z) and Z_g = integral exp(g(z)) dmu(z), and let mu_f = mu.tilted(f) and mu_g = mu.tilted(g), the normalized exponential reweightings specified by the tilted-measure construction. Then the selected measurable real log-likelihood-ratio representative llr(mu_f,mu_g) satisfies llr(mu_f,mu_g)(x) = f(x)-log(Z_f)-g(x)+log(Z_g) for mu_f-almost every x. Here exp and log are the real exponential and the Lean real logarithm. The almost-everywhere reference measure is mu_f, not an unstated background probability measure. No separate global measurability assumption on g, nonzero-mass assumption on mu, or positive-normalizer assumption is imposed; the statement uses the Lean constructions also in degenerate cases and does not assert a pointwise identity.

import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.InformationTheory.RNLogRatio
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Calculus
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Measure.Tilted
import Mathlib.Tactic

/-!
# Smooth representatives of log-density ratios between tilted measures

Mathlib's `llr` is the canonical measurable Radon--Nikodym representative.  A
paper calculation may instead differentiate an explicit smooth representative.
This file keeps those two roles separate: it proves almost-everywhere agreement
with the canonical `llr`, then differentiates the explicit representative.

The quadratic specialization is equation (11) in Lee--Shen--Tian,
arXiv:2010.03106v4, used by SPHMC Lemma 4.17.  It does not prove a
log-Sobolev, Talagrand, Fisher-information, or Wasserstein inequality.
-/

namespace AutoSamplingTheory
namespace TechnicalLemmas
namespace InformationTheory
namespace TiltedLogRatio

open MeasureTheory
open scoped ENNReal NNReal

noncomputable section

variable {X : Type*} [MeasurableSpace X]

/-- The explicit log-density-ratio representative between two exponential
tilts of the same base measure. -/
private def representative (mu : Measure X) (f g : X → ℝ) (x : X) : ℝ :=
  f x - Real.log (∫ z, Real.exp (f z) ∂mu) - g x +
    Real.log (∫ z, Real.exp (g z) ∂mu)

/-- The canonical `llr` between two integrable tilts agrees almost everywhere
with the explicit difference of exponents and log normalizers.

The equality is stated under the left tilted law, which is the measure used by
relative Fisher information. -/
theorem llr_tilted_tilted_ae
    (mu : Measure X) [SigmaFinite mu] (f g : X → ℝ)
    (hf : Measurable f)
    (hfi : Integrable (fun x => Real.exp (f x)) mu)
    (hgi : Integrable (fun x => Real.exp (g x)) mu) :
    MeasureTheory.llr (mu.tilted f) (mu.tilted g) =ᵐ[mu.tilted f]
      fun x => f x - Real.log (∫ z, Real.exp (f z) ∂mu) - g x +
        Real.log (∫ z, Real.exp (g z) ∂mu) := by
  have hbase :
      MeasureTheory.llr (mu.tilted f) (mu.tilted g) =ᵐ[mu]
        representative mu f g := by
    filter_upwards [
      MeasureTheory.llr_tilted_left
        (μ := mu) (ν := mu.tilted g) (f := f)
        (absolutelyContinuous_tilted hgi) hfi hf.aemeasurable,
      MeasureTheory.llr_tilted_right
        (μ := mu) (ν := mu) (f := g)
        Measure.AbsolutelyContinuous.rfl hgi,
      MeasureTheory.llr_self mu] with x hleft hright hself
    rw [hleft, hright, hself]
    simp [representative]
    ring
  exact (tilted_absolutelyContinuous mu f).ae_eq hbase

section Quadratic

variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [CompleteSpace E]
  [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]

/-- The negative quadratic exponent in a restricted Gaussian fiber. -/
private def quadraticExponent (eta : ℝ) (y x : E) : ℝ :=
  -(‖x - y‖ ^ 2 / (2 * eta))

omit [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E] in
private theorem quadraticExponent_measurable (eta : ℝ) (y : E) :
    Measurable (quadraticExponent eta y) := by
  change Measurable (fun x : E => -(‖x - y‖ ^ 2 / (2 * eta)))
  fun_prop

omit [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] in
private theorem hasGradientAt_quadraticExponent
    {eta : ℝ} (heta : eta ≠ 0) (y x : E) :
    HasGradientAt (quadraticExponent eta y) (-eta⁻¹ • (x - y)) x := by
  rw [hasGradientAt_iff_hasFDerivAt]
  have hfun : quadraticExponent eta y =
      fun t : E => (-eta⁻¹ / 2) * ‖t - y‖ ^ 2 := by
    funext t
    simp only [quadraticExponent]
    field_simp [heta]
  have hq : HasFDerivAt (fun t : E => (-eta⁻¹ / 2) * ‖t - y‖ ^ 2)
      ((-eta⁻¹) • innerSL ℝ (x - y)) x := by
    convert (((hasFDerivAt_id x).sub_const y).norm_sq).const_mul (-eta⁻¹ / 2)
      using 1 <;> first | rfl | (ext v; simp; ring)
  rw [hfun]
  have hdual :
      InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ E (-eta⁻¹ • (x - y)) =
        (-eta⁻¹) • innerSL ℝ (x - y) := by
    ext v
    simp [InnerProductSpace.toDual_apply_apply]
  rw [hdual]
  exact hq

omit [BorelSpace E] in
/-- The smooth representative of the log-density ratio between two restricted
Gaussian fibers has the constant score `(y-y') / eta`.

This is the differential identity in Lee--Shen--Tian equation (11).  The
normalizing constants are retained in `representative`; they disappear only
because they are constant in the spatial variable. -/
theorem gradient_quadratic_representative
    (mu : Measure E) {eta : ℝ} (heta : eta ≠ 0) (y y' x : E) :
    gradient
        (fun t =>
          -(‖t - y‖ ^ 2 / (2 * eta)) -
            Real.log (∫ z, Real.exp (-(‖z - y‖ ^ 2 / (2 * eta))) ∂mu) -
          (-(‖t - y'‖ ^ 2 / (2 * eta))) +
            Real.log (∫ z, Real.exp (-(‖z - y'‖ ^ 2 / (2 * eta))) ∂mu)) x =
      eta⁻¹ • (y - y') := by
  have hy := hasGradientAt_quadraticExponent heta y x
  have hy' := hasGradientAt_quadraticExponent heta y' x
  apply HasGradientAt.gradient
  rw [hasGradientAt_iff_hasFDerivAt]
  change HasFDerivAt
    (fun t => quadraticExponent eta y t -
      Real.log (∫ z, Real.exp (quadraticExponent eta y z) ∂mu) -
      quadraticExponent eta y' t +
      Real.log (∫ z, Real.exp (quadraticExponent eta y' z) ∂mu))
    (InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ E (eta⁻¹ • (y - y'))) x
  let c := Real.log (∫ z, Real.exp (quadraticExponent eta y z) ∂mu)
  let c' := Real.log (∫ z, Real.exp (quadraticExponent eta y' z) ∂mu)
  have hderiv : HasFDerivAt
      (fun t => quadraticExponent eta y t - c - quadraticExponent eta y' t + c')
      ((InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ E (-eta⁻¹ • (x - y))) -
        InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ E (-eta⁻¹ • (x - y'))) x :=
    ((hy.hasFDerivAt.sub_const c).sub hy'.hasFDerivAt).add_const c'
  have hvec :
      (-eta⁻¹ • (x - y)) - (-eta⁻¹ • (x - y')) =
        eta⁻¹ • (y - y') := by
    module
  rw [← hvec, map_sub]
  simpa only [c, c'] using hderiv

end Quadratic

end

end TiltedLogRatio
end InformationTheory
end TechnicalLemmas
end AutoSamplingTheory

candidate_publication_context.statement: For normalized restricted-Gaussian fibers, the canonical log-likelihood ratio agrees almost everywhere under the left fiber with the explicit normalized quadratic exponent difference. For eta>0 the displayed smooth representative has the constant spatial gradient eta^{-1}(y-y'). This is the score calculation in the cited contraction proof, not the contraction itself.
assumptions: The canonical llr identity uses a sigma-finite common base, a measurable left exponent and integrability of both exponential weights.
The source fiber uses eta>0; the reusable calculus theorem only requires eta nonzero.
Almost-everywhere value equality is not converted into differentiability of the canonical measurable representative.

obligations.label: Identify the explicit normalized tilt ratio a.e. with the canonical llr
Prove the exact constant gradient of the displayed smooth representative

lesson.title: Canonical llr equals the explicit normalized tilt ratio a.e.
lesson.statement: For a σ-finite base μ and two integrable exponential tilts, Mathlib's canonical log-likelihood ratio of the f-tilt against the g-tilt agrees almost everywhere under the left tilted law with f−log Z_f−g+log Z_g.
assumptions: The common base μ is σ-finite.
f is measurable and both exp f and exp g are μ-integrable.
The equality is under the left tilt μ_f, which is the law used by relative Fisher information.

steps.title: Expand the left tilt
steps.text: Mathlib's left-tilt identity contributes f−log Z_f and leaves a base-to-right-tilt llr.

steps.title: Expand the right tilt
steps.text: The right-tilt identity contributes −g+log Z_g, while the self log ratio is zero.

steps.title: Transfer the null set
steps.text: The equality is first assembled μ-a.e. and then transported to μ_f because every tilted measure is absolutely continuous with respect to its base.

lesson.lean_statement: The right-hand side is written explicitly in the public theorem, so no hidden selected representative occurs in its interface.
lesson.lean_proof: The proof combines the three canonical Mathlib llr identities pointwise on a full-measure set and uses absolute continuity to change the a.e. measure.
